text:
maya: Heads-up: started seeing a p99 latency jump for gpt-medium-quant in prod at ~10:12 UTC. p50 looks fine, but p99 jumped from ~220ms -> ~600ms. Traces point at long GPU kernel stalls during attention steps.

perf-bot: automated-profile: window=10m, pool=gpu-pool-3, avg_gpu_util=0.78, p99_lat=605ms, kernel_hotspot=attn_fused_v2 (3.1x slower than baseline), fallback_kernel=attn_unfused, kvcache_hit_rate dropped 4%.

maya: quick snapshot from node-13 logs:```
[2026-02-28T10:11:55Z] CALL start id=abc123 model=gpt-medium-quant seq=512 microbatch=8
[2026-02-28T10:11:55Z] kernel: attn_fused_v2 launch time=12ms
[2026-02-28T10:11:56Z] kernel stall wait_for_mem=480ms
[2026-02-28T10:11:56Z] fallback to attn_unfused launch time=7ms
```

alex: this smells like the selector change from #PR-4826 that promoted attn_fused_v2 for medium models. hash=9b3f2c1. We saw perf wins in microbench, but maybe tail behaviour on mixed seq lengths is worse. :thinking_face:

li: also worth noting: the recent batching tweak increased default microbatch target from 4->8 for seq>=256 (config: batching.default_microbatch=8). That increases KV cache pressure leading to evictions for long context streams. If KV miss increases, we pay memcopy + recompute in attention -> stalls.

devon: agreed. Two levers: revert kernel selector OR change batching heuristics to cap microbatch at 4 for seq in [256..1024]. Reverting kernel selector is safer for short-term rollback.

samir: long-term we should avoid hard-coded microbatch jumps. Suggest dynamic microbatching: target_based on running p95 and kv_hit_rate. If kv_hit_rate<0.95, force microbatch<=4. Also consider headroom target change from util=0.75 -> 0.65 to avoid saturation tails.

alex: quick micro-profiling on canary (local reproduce): with microbatch=8, p99=620ms; microbatch=4, p99=280ms. Kernel attn_fused_v2 p99=480ms vs unfused p99=260ms. So both kernel and microbatch play roles.

maya: operational suggestion: 1) rollback kernel selector in canary, 2) apply a temporary batching cap on prod route (microbatch_max=4) for 10% traffic, 3) schedule load-shed policy if p99>500ms for >2m. Anyone see issues?

devon: :+1: on canary. For headroom, I want to test target_util=0.65 on canary GPUS; we can measure throughput loss vs tail improvement. I suspect throughput ~-6% but p99 improves ~40-50%.

li: note: kvcache eviction metric is noisy. For the test, pin a workload with long-context chat (seq=1024, many small turns) to stress kvcache. Also enable per-request debug tag so we can correlate evictions->latency.

samir: we should also prepare fallback route to smaller model (gpt-small-quant) with quality degrade thresholds: if route avg_p99 > 450ms for 1m, shift 5% traffic to gpt-small. That avoids blackholing.

perf-bot: alpha-profile-report (post-discussion run): canary rollback selector + batching_cap=4 -> canary p99=290ms, avg_gpu_util=0.66, throughput change -5%. Detailed diff: attn_fused_v2 use down 92% -> 12%. kvcache_hit_rate up +3.8%.

maya: perfect. I'll open a rollback PR for selector (link: https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/4941) and a runtime config change for batching cap. Will spin up canary with target_util=0.65 and fallback route to gpt-small.

oncall-bot: scheduled-canary: id=canary-176870-c1 start=10:45UTC scope=10% traffic nodes=gpu-pool-3 config={microbatch_max:4, target_util:0.65, selector:rollback-9b3f2c1}.

alex: add a quick postmortem checklist item: 1) add selector A/B tests in bench harness for mixed-seq workloads, 2) extend kernel tail latency tests (p99/p999), 3) surface kvcache evictions in route dashboards.

maya: noted. I'll update the runbook and ping infra to make headroom tuning easier. Thanks all. :eyes: :shipit:

samir: follow-up: let's land the dynamic microbatching RFC next week. I'll draft it and include simulation results for util targets 0.6/0.65/0.7.

maya: closing loop — monitoring will alert if canary p99 > 450ms after change. We'll reconvene if we see anomalies.
